group.passage:
There’s no denying that parenting styles affect children to a great degree, with the influences continuing well into adulthood. Self-absorbed parents, for one, are likely to bring up children with emotion or relationship issues. By definition, being self-absorbed means being interested in only oneself or his or her own activities and interests. Self-absorbed parents tend to overlook their children’s emotional and psychological needs and will ensure they’re in the spotlight of people’s admiration and attention because of their children. __❶__ Their children, overwhelmed with parental expectations and demands, are like trophies or prizes on display, meant to win them more envy and recognition from others.
Children of such parents will most likely suffer psychological consequences, reacting differently depending on their personality. Omnipotent children, on one hand, spare no effort to fulfill their parents’ demands, driven by their deep-rooted belief that they are obligated to satisfy their parents. However, when they fall short, they become their own worst critics, often falling victim to depression, anxiety, and other mental disorders. Impotent children, in contrast, are as self-absorbed as their parents, if not more. They can be either high academic achievers or school dropouts, but usually share an unstable relationship with their parents. Heated arguments often end up with physical or verbal abuse and conflicts, with neither side willing to give in. Such children are usually at odds with their siblings and peers as well, because of their selfish and aggressive tendencies.
Unfortunately, kids’ parental relationships often have a considerable impact on how they treat or interact with others, even in adulthood. If left untreated, those issues will poison an otherwise healthy relationship. Since people may not always be conscious of how they have been conditioned by their parents and how they respond accordingly, we as friends or family will do well to suggest that they seek help if we spot some red flags in their words or behaviors.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is best placed in __❶__?

options.A: It is quite considerate of them to stand in their children’s shoes and to make changes to their daily schedule as they see fit.
options.B: More often than not, they register their kids for expensive lessons to boost their academic performance or extracurricular record.
options.C: Such parents are unlikely to share a close relationship with their spouse, who may be fully committed to his or her professional work.
options.D: They see nothing wrong in calling their kids’ teachers numerous times a day just to make sure they are not bullied by their peers.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is most likely to be made by an omnipotent kid?

options.A: “I doubt I’d ever have the courage to stand up for myself, though I believe I’m responsible for my own life, and that I’m the one in charge.”
options.B: “I can’t care less about what they think of me. I’m entitled to my own opinions and there’s no way they are going to stand in my way.”
options.C: “Someday I’m going to make them pay for their abusive behavior towards me. I’m not supposed to be treated this way.”
options.D: “There’s no way I will let them down; I will prove to them that I’m the most deserving one of all their children.”

questions.stem: What is the purpose of this passage?

options.A: To discuss results of a parenting style and call for action.
options.B: To alert teachers to possible setbacks in their teaching career.
options.C: To advise teenagers on how to get along with their parents.
options.D: To invite parents to have a sincere discussion with their kids.

tags.topic: effects of self-absorbed parents on their children
